title: Ops signal fusion: enriched PD notifications and Slack-thread reconciliation
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a lightweight 'Ops Signal Fusion' service that enriches PagerDuty incidents and Slack incident threads with compact, high-signal telemetry bundles (trace snippets, latency histograms, top error logs, and a ranked set of candidate runbook sections). The goal is to reduce mean time to identification (MTTI) for oncall by surfacing the minimal evidence needed to form a hypothesis, and to seed postmortems when incidents resolve.
background: Current PD and Slack integrations attach generic links and full traces; responders still need to hunt across traces, dashboards, and logs. Multiple postmortems show delays in initial causal hypothesis due to noisy attachments and missing quicklinks to the right spans and error samples. We already have trace extraction hooks and log sample APIs, but no unified attachment composer that produces concise bundles tailored to severity and SLO impact.
goals: Attach a compact evidence bundle to PD alerts and the primary Slack thread within 10s of alert creation
Provide a ranked list of 3 candidate runbook sections with direct jump links
Seed a draft postmortem doc (template + timeline + top 5 signals) when an incident is resolved
Preserve PII-sensitive fields by applying configurable redaction rules
Respect RBAC and tenant isolation for Dedicated/Private deployments
non_goals: Full automated remediation (out of scope for this ticket)
Replacing long-form traces or full log dumps; we produce summaries and deep-links only
solution_overview: Introduce a microservice (ops-signal-fusion) that listens to incident events from the orchestration bus, queries the trace hook service for top spans, queries the metrics pipeline for latency percentiles and anomaly flags, and fetches a small set of recent log error samples. The composer runs a lightweight ranking model to pick the most relevant artifacts and generates compact attachments for PD and Slack (JSON+markdown). It also writes a postmortem seed to Drive/Confluence when an incident is closed, optionally creating a draft doc via the existing postmortem service API.
tradeoffs: Synchronous vs asynchronous enrichment: synchronous attachment provides the fastest UX but increases alert latency. We'll use an async-first model with a 10s soft window and a 30s fallback to attach what is available.
Attachment size vs signal richness: to avoid notification noise, limit attachments to 1-2KB summary and up to 3 deep-link artifacts; full artifacts remain in storage and are linked.
Ranking model complexity: start with a rules-and-features linear scorer (latency contribution, error count, span duration) and iterate; heavier ML ranking deferred to later cycles.
Privacy: we apply redaction s in composer; sensitive fields are masked by default and configurable per tenant (security review required).
implementation_plan: Schema: define 'evidence-bundle' JSON schema (summary, top_spans[], latency_summary, log_samples[], runbook_candidates[])
Service: implement ops-signal-fusion microservice with two endpoints: /compose and websocket/listen for incident events
Integrations: add PD attachment composer using PD API v2 (respecting PD attachment size limits) and Slack thread composer using block-kit rapid snippets
Trace hooks: add a lightweight 'top-spans' query to trace-store with a 500ms budget per query
Metrics: implement percentile snapshot and anomaly flag from metrics pipeline; cache hot snapshots in Redis for 15s
Runbooks: index runbook fragments by signal tags (error type, service, metric) and return top 3 candidates
Postmortem seed: call postmortem service to create a draft document on incident close with timeline, evidence bundle, and suggested RCA owners
Observability: instrument ops-signal-fusion with SLOs and internal traces; emit compose_latency, attach_success, attach_size, and redaction_rate
milestones: Slack thread composer and runbook candidate ranking — 2025-02-04
Canary rollout to staging and Dedicated customers — 2025-02-18
acceptance_criteria: When a PD alert fires, the PD incident receives an evidence bundle attachment within 30s in 95% of cases
Slack incident thread receives the same bundle in the primary thread in 95% of cases
Seeded postmortem draft is created automatically for incidents marked Sev 2+
Compose latency median < 300ms when data is available in cache; p95 < 5s
No sensitive fields are leaked in attachments for tenants with redaction enabled (verified by security test)
testing_plan: Unit tests for composer ranking logic and redaction rules
Integration tests with a PD sandbox and a Slack test workspace
Load test: simulate 100 concurrent incidents per second to validate compose queue and Redis cache
Chaos test: simulate trace-store timeouts and ensure attachments degrade gracefully
Security test: run redaction verification with sample PII payloads
monitoring_and_slo: Compose latency SLO: median < 300ms, p95 < 5s. Attachment success rate SLO: 99.5% over rolling 7d. Metric dashboards: ops-signal-fusion/compose-latency, ops-signal-fusion/attach-errors, ops-signal-fusion/queued-events. Alerting: page on attach_success < 99% for 30m and compose latency p95 > 10s for 15m.
rollout_strategy: Start with internal staging incidents, then enable for 10% of PD incidents in staging with canary tagging. Next, opt-in Dedicated customers with explicit consent and allow tenant-level configuration. Gradual ramp to 100% over 2 weeks while monitoring attach metrics and false positive runbook suggestions.
manual_rollout_steps: Deploy service to staging and enable composer stub
Run PD sandbox e2e and validate attachments
Enable Slack composer in a test workspace and validate block-kit rendering
Open canary flag and route 10% of incidents through composer
Monitor dashboards and runbook suggestion precision metrics
open_questions: What privacy standards do enterprise customers require for redaction configuration? (ask security/compliance)
Should attachments be encrypted at rest separately from tenant storage?
Do we include sampled stack traces for internal errors, or only span context and logs?
What is the maximum PD attachment size we should target for all supported PD plans?
